about.title: About
about.description: Valerio Colapinto, Electronic Engineering student at Sapienza: why and how I write these study sites.
about.h1b: I build the tools I study with.
about.lead: Electronic Engineering student at Sapienza, graduating in 2028. I am interested in electronics, telecommunications and computer science.
about.facts.title: At a glance
about.f4.v: Interactive study tools, free and tracking-free
about.how.title: Understand from scratch, then verify
about.how.p: These sites come from the way I like to study: understand things from scratch, check them with exercises and simulations, and build the tools I need.
about.s1.d: I start from definitions and proofs, not from formulas to memorise.
about.s2.d: Where possible, every exercise has a computed solution checked with a second method, so the result can be trusted.
about.s3.d: If a tool does not exist, I write it: exercise generators, mock-exam simulators, formula sheets.
about.work.title: Git, GitHub and an AI assistant
about.work.p: I develop with Git and GitHub and with the help of artificial intelligence. The code is public and, where possible, the content is verified with automated tests.
about.pr.title: What you will find here (and what not)
about.p1.d: Explanations, exercises and quizzes are original: no exam texts or professors' materials.
about.p2.d: No accounts, cookies or analytics: your progress stays in your browser.
about.p3.d: The code is public on GitHub under the MIT licence.
about.p4.d: They are not affiliated with any university or professor: for syllabus and exams, official sources prevail.
about.ct.title: Contact
about.ct.sub: For questions, errors you found on the sites or content removal requests, email is the most direct channel.

contribute.title: Contribute
contribute.description: Report an error or suggest an explanation, an exercise or an improvement to the study sites.
contribute.lead: Found an error, an unclear explanation or a missing exercise? Every report is read and, if correct, the site is updated.
contribute.tip1: name the page and, if you can, the exact formula or step;
contribute.tip2: explain what you expected and what you found;
contribute.tip3: if you want to be listed in the acknowledgements, write the name to use.
